templates.name: CloudPanel (Example Music)
templates.description:
Companion template for ansible/playbooks/cloudpanel/site.yml. Copied from zabbix_template_linuxtools.json's own generator (Robert's established pattern for this series) and expanded, 2026-10-19. Flat, native, one-item-per-thing design, same discipline as every other template in this series.

SECTIONS
  Packages: one item+trigger per package from 10-packages.yml/00-preflight.yml/30-cloudpanel.yml, plain vfs.file.exists against /usr/share/doc/<pkg>/copyright. curl/wget deliberately excluded -- already checked by the linuxtools template. The database engine package is macro-driven ({$CLOUDPANEL.DB_PACKAGE}) rather than one item per possible cloudpanel_db_engine value -- only 3 distinct real package names exist across all 7 engine choices (checked directly against cloudpanel_db_matrix, not assumed): percona-server-server-5.7 (MYSQL_5.7, Debian 11 only), percona-server-server (MYSQL_8.0 or MYSQL_8.4 -- identical package name), mariadb-server (any MARIADB_10.6/10.11/11.4/11.8/12.3).
  Listeners: net.tcp.port against 8443 (CloudPanel web UI) and 3306 (the database engine, always expected regardless of which engine is installed) -- a genuine TCP connect check via the agent's own native key, not a file-based proxy for it.
  Swap config: macro-gated ({$CLOUDPANEL.SWAP_ENABLED}, default "yes") -- /etc/dphys-swapfile's CONF_SWAPFILE line is only written when cloudpanel_swap_enabled is true, so the trigger only fires when the macro says swap is expected to be on. Set {$CLOUDPANEL.SWAP_ENABLED}="no" per-host to match a host where cloudpanel_swap_enabled was set false at install time.
  Static IP / network: the cloudpanel-static NetworkManager profile's mere existence (vfs.file.exists -- works without read permission, the file is mode 0600 root:root) plus a separate nmcli-based read of its configured IP4.METHOD (manual=static, auto=DHCP) -- NOT a file content read, since the agent user can't read a 0600 root-owned file; nmcli queries NetworkManager's own running daemon over D-Bus instead, a different, read-permitted access path. This specific permission boundary is REASONED, not live-verified against a real zabbix-agent user (the test box was unreachable when this template was built) -- confirm on first import. Visibility only, no trigger -- whether the static IP is actually activated live is a separate, deliberate per-host decision (00-preflight.yml's own gated activate-now question), not a single correct state to alert on.
  CloudPanel footprint: /home/clp/htdocs/app/files (the exact directory cloudpanel's own postinst itself checks to decide fresh-install vs. update -- the authoritative 'is CloudPanel installed' signal), /home/clp/htdocs/app/data/db.sq3 (CloudPanel's own internal SQLite app database -- NOT the MySQL/MariaDB engine it manages for customer sites, confirmed via the real .env's DATABASE_URL), and the clp user's /etc/passwd line (visibility only).
  nodeinfo.json contents: identical pattern to linuxtools' own template -- a vfs.file.contents master item ({$NODEINFO.MAXAGE} nodata staleness trigger) with DEPENDENT items for every field in tasks/nodeinfo.yml's base schema, extracted via JSONPATH. No role-specific nodeinfo_extra fields exist for this family (confirmed by reading all 5 playbook files) -- unlike firewall/ansible-node, there's nothing CloudPanel-specific to extract here beyond the base schema.

NOT YET LIVE-IMPORTED OR LIVE-TESTED against a real Zabbix server or a real zabbix-agent -- same status as every other template in this series as of 2026-10-19, pending Robert's own test pass.

IMPORT: configuration.import, rules: createMissing+updateExisting+deleteMissing on items/triggers, createMissing+updateExisting on template_groups/templates.

items.name: Package installed: database engine
items.description: 1 if /usr/share/doc/{$CLOUDPANEL.DB_PACKAGE}/copyright exists. Package name depends on cloudpanel_db_engine (set at install time, see group_vars/cloudpanel_servers/main.yml's cloudpanel_db_matrix) -- set the {$CLOUDPANEL.DB_PACKAGE} macro to match. Real values seen in the matrix: percona-server-server-5.7 (MYSQL_5.7, Debian 11 only), percona-server-server (MYSQL_8.0 or MYSQL_8.4 -- identical package name, different repo/version), mariadb-server (any MARIADB_10.6/10.11/11.4/11.8/12.3).

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing its database engine package ({$CLOUDPANEL.DB_PACKAGE})
triggers.description: The database engine package named by {$CLOUDPANEL.DB_PACKAGE} isn't installed (or the macro doesn't match what was actually installed -- check cloudpanel_db_engine). Re-run cloudpanel/site.yml.

items.name: CloudPanel web UI listening (8443)
items.description: 1 if a TCP connection to port 8443 succeeds (CloudPanel's own web UI). 30-cloudpanel.yml's own 'Assert CloudPanel is actually listening on 8443' task checks this once at install time; this item checks it on an ongoing basis.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - CloudPanel web UI (8443) is not listening
triggers.description: Port 8443 isn't accepting connections. Check clp-nginx/clp-php-fpm service status.

items.name: Database engine listening (3306)
items.description: 1 if a TCP connection to port 3306 succeeds (MySQL/MariaDB, whichever engine this host uses -- always expected, the database isn't an optional component of a CloudPanel install the way swap is).

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - database engine (3306) is not listening
triggers.description: Port 3306 isn't accepting connections. Check the mysql/mariadb service status.

items.name: Swap config: CONF_SWAPFILE line
items.description: The matched CONF_SWAPFILE line from /etc/dphys-swapfile, if present. Only written when cloudpanel_swap_enabled is true (10-packages.yml's own 'when:' guard) -- the trigger only fires if {$CLOUDPANEL.SWAP_ENABLED}="yes", same macro-text-comparison pattern, so a host with swap deliberately disabled never alerts on this file being absent.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - swap config missing/wrong in /etc/dphys-swapfile
triggers.description: cloudpanel_swap_enabled is true (per {$CLOUDPANEL.SWAP_ENABLED}) but /etc/dphys-swapfile's CONF_SWAPFILE line doesn't match. Re-run cloudpanel/site.yml's 10-packages.yml.

items.name: File exists: cloudpanel-static NetworkManager profile
items.description: 1 if the cloudpanel-static .nmconnection profile exists. File itself is mode 0600 root:root (00-preflight.yml's own template task) -- this existence check works for any user (stat doesn't need read permission), but the CONTENTS aren't readable by zabbix-agent, hence the separate nmcli-based item below instead of a vfs.file.regexp against the file.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing the cloudpanel-static NetworkManager profile
triggers.description: Re-run cloudpanel/site.yml's 00-preflight.yml -- see its 'Write cloudpanel-static NetworkManager connection profile' task.

items.name: Static IP: configured method (manual=static, auto=DHCP)
items.description: Reads the cloudpanel-static profile's own configured IP4.METHOD via nmcli -- NOT a file read (the .nmconnection file is mode 0600, unreadable by an unprivileged zabbix-agent user; nmcli queries NetworkManager's running daemon over D-Bus instead, a different access path that doesn't need file read permission for read-only queries, per NetworkManager's own standard D-Bus policy). Expected value: 'manual' (static IP configured, per cloudpanel_static_ip). UNVERIFIED against a real zabbix-agent user on a real box -- reasoned from NetworkManager's documented permission model, not live-tested (box was unreachable when this template was built). Visibility only, no trigger -- whether this profile is activated live is a separate, deliberate per-host decision (00-preflight.yml's own gated activate-now question), not something with one single correct state to alert on.

items.name: Directory exists: /home/clp/htdocs/app/files
items.description: 1 if /home/clp/htdocs/app/files exists as a directory. This is the exact marker cloudpanel's own postinst checks (`[ ! -d /home/clp/htdocs/app/files ]`) to decide fresh-install vs. update -- the authoritative 'is CloudPanel actually installed' signal, confirmed by reading that script directly.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing /home/clp/htdocs/app/files
triggers.description: CloudPanel's own install directory is missing. Re-run cloudpanel/site.yml.

items.name: File exists: CloudPanel's own app database (SQLite)
items.description: 1 if /home/clp/htdocs/app/data/db.sq3 exists -- CloudPanel's own internal app metadata (users, sites, the database_server registry clpctl db:show:master-credentials reads from). NOT the MySQL/MariaDB engine this host manages for customer sites -- confirmed by reading the real .env (DATABASE_URL=sqlite:////home/clp/htdocs/app/data/db.sq3), a completely separate store. Depends on the install-directory trigger.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing CloudPanel's own app database
triggers.description: CloudPanel's own SQLite app database is missing -- the web UI/clpctl won't function at all. Re-run cloudpanel/site.yml.

items.name: clp user's /etc/passwd line
items.description: The full matched /etc/passwd line for the clp user (created by the cloudpanel package's own postinst, owns /home/clp/). Visibility only -- see the exists trigger above for the real pass/fail signal; this is for diagnosis if that one fires.

items.name: File exists: /etc/example-music/nodeinfo.json
items.description: 1 if nodeinfo.json exists. Every properly-built host is EXA[ROLE][SITE][NNN]-conformant, so this should never legitimately be 0.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing /etc/example-music/nodeinfo.json
triggers.description: Re-run cloudpanel/site.yml. If this fires, something is wrong with the host's own hostname/build, not just a missing file.

items.name: nodeinfo.json contents (master)
items.description: Raw nodeinfo.json content -- master item for every examplemusic.nodeinfo.* dependent item below. Staleness (nodata) trigger depends on the exists trigger above -- a missing file would eventually go stale too, same root cause, one alert.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} hasn't had cloudpanel/site.yml run in {$NODEINFO.MAXAGE}
triggers.description: nodeinfo.json hasn't been rewritten within {$NODEINFO.MAXAGE} -- cloudpanel/site.yml hasn't run against this host recently.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME}'s nodeinfo.json says ansible_managed=false
triggers.description: nodeinfo.json's ansible_managed field is false -- something wrote this file outside Ansible.

items.name: nodeinfo: environment
items.description: Drift detector -- fires if this host's recorded environment changed since the previous cloudpanel/site.yml run (could be intentional, e.g. a real promotion -- check before treating as a fault).

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME}'s nodeinfo environment changed ({ITEM.LASTVALUE})
triggers.description: environment in nodeinfo.json differs from the previous recorded run.

macros.description: How long nodeinfo.json can go without a fresh write before the staleness trigger fires. Override per-host if a host is deliberately on a less frequent Ansible run schedule.

The real apt package name providing this host's chosen cloudpanel_db_engine (group_vars/cloudpanel_servers/main.yml's cloudpanel_db_matrix). Default here matches install.sh's own default engine (MYSQL_8.4). Real values: percona-server-server-5.7 (MYSQL_5.7, Debian 11 only); percona-server-server (MYSQL_8.0 or MYSQL_8.4); mariadb-server (any MARIADB_10.6/10.11/11.4/11.8/12.3).

Whether this host's cloudpanel_swap_enabled was true at install time (10-packages.yml). Default "yes" matches that variable's own default. Valid values: "yes" or "no" -- set to "no" per-host if swap was deliberately disabled, so the swap-config trigger doesn't fire on a host that never wrote the file on purpose.
